case.case_title: Kapugeekiyana v. Hettiarachchi and Two Others
case.source_citation: Supreme Court of Sri Lanka, S.C. No. 80/84, decided on 8 August 1984

clause.text: Any person detained shall be brought before a judge and cannot be held without legal order.

case_context.legal_issue: Whether the petitioner was held in custody or detained without being brought before a judge of the nearest competent court within the time prescribed by law, violating Article 13(2).
case_context.petitioner_claim: The petitioner claimed he was arrested on 13 June 1984 and illegally detained incommunicado on the 4th floor of the C.I.D. office until 17 June without being produced before a judge, violating Article 13(2).
case_context.respondent_argument: The respondents claimed the petitioner was arrested on 16 June and produced before the Magistrate on 17 June, thus no violation occurred.
key_facts: Petitioner was allegedly arrested on 13 June at about 9:00 a.m.
Petitioner was held incommunicado on the 4th floor of the C.I.D. office until 17 June.
Petitioner was produced before the Acting Magistrate on 17 June and remanded.
Respondents denied arrest on 13 June and claimed arrest on 16 June.
Independent evidence including complaints by petitioner's wife and affidavits supported arrest on 13 June.

reasoning.interpretation_summary: Article 13(2) requires that any person detained must be brought before a judge of the nearest competent court according to procedure established by law, and cannot be held in custody without legal order beyond a reasonable time, generally not exceeding 24 hours as per the Code of Criminal Procedure.
reasoning.application_to_facts: The Court found credible independent evidence that the petitioner was arrested on 13 June and illegally detained until 17 June without being produced before a judge, violating Article 13(2) and sections 36 and 37 of the Code of Criminal Procedure Act No. 15 of 1979.
principles_established: Detention without production before a judge within 24 hours violates Article 13(2).
The procedure established by law includes sections 36 and 37 of the Code of Criminal Procedure.
Independent evidence can establish the date of arrest and detention.
precedents_cited: A. K. Velmurugu v. The Attorney-General S.C. Application No. 74/81

outcome.holding: The Court held that the petitioner was illegally detained for three days without being produced before a judge, violating Article 13(2). Compensation of Rs. 10,000 was awarded.
outcome.remedy_or_orders: Order for respondents to pay Rs. 10,000 as compensation to petitioner.

link_explanation.why_this_clause_matters: Article 13(2) was central to the Court's finding of illegal detention and the award of compensation for violation of the petitioner's fundamental rights.

evidence.evidence_excerpt: Independent evidence including affidavits and complaints established that the petitioner was arrested on 13 June and detained until 17 June without being produced before a judge, violating Article 13(2).
